rationale:
ROUND 2 of 7ba5b8c4. Round 1 was REVISE: 5 approve / 3 object, unreadable:0 (so a real verdict, not the harness). Nine objections, every one answerable with a check, and TWO OF THEM FOUND CONCRETE DEFECTS. Both are fixed below and both are recorded rather than quietly corrected.

DEFECT 1, and it is the one that would have shipped wrong -- editquality (low, edit 5) objected that the concept-register glob was asserted by analogy rather than measured, and that 'if the path is wrong the fix silently omits one of the four named durable sources while still reporting success'. IT WAS WRONG. Measured: docs/agent_docs/docs026_concept_register/*.md matches 28 files, all of them top-level PLANNING docs (001_PROMPT_charter.md, 002_PLAN_extraction.md, 003_TAXONOMY_seed.md, PILOT_*, SUMMARY_where_we_are_*) -- exactly the superseded-by-design class this plan's whole scope argument excludes. The actual register is docs/agent_docs/docs026_concept_register/register/*.md: 110 entry files. So the submitted glob would have indexed the wrong half of that source AND poisoned the corpus with the stale-doc class, while the VERIFY reported success. Corrected to register/*.md.

DEFECT 2 -- reuse_agent (medium, edit 2) objected that no search for an existing section-splitter was claimed. Searched now: platform/orchestration/actions/rag_actions.go:396 `func chunkContent(content string, chunkSize, overlap int) []string` is the platform's only text chunker. It is a FIXED-WIDTH CHARACTER WINDOW with overlap, not a heading splitter, and code_symbols_actions.go's own header already records why it is unused here: 'chunkContent fragments code, so it is not used here'. For markdown a character window splits mid-section and destroys the heading->section mapping, which IS the unit this plan indexes. So: searched, found, and deliberately not reused, for a stated reason rather than by omission.

THE TWO MEDIUM PLUMBING OBJECTIONS ARE ANSWERED WITH FILE:LINE AND WITH RUNTIME EVIDENCE. editquality (medium, edit 4) was right to demand it -- 'this is exactly the class of unverified plumbing that sank the prior approved plan' -- and that is the correct standard to hold this workstream to. (a) internal/reposource/github_source.go:196-245: the extraction loop walks every tar entry, establishes the top-level prefix, applies a path-traversal guard and a 64<<20 per-file limit, and writes every TypeDir/TypeReg. THERE IS NO PATH FILTER OF ANY KIND. (b) analyse_repo_local_action.go:165 fetches to `dir`, :197 calls AnalyseWithExclude(dir, excludes), and :285 sets defaultAnalyseExcludePatterns = []string{"docs/"} -- an ANALYSER-walk exclude, applied after everything is already on disk. (c) internal/analysis/types.go:9 `Root string \`json:"root"\`` survives the JSON round-trip through collected_data. (d) RUNTIME, not inference: the layer-1 indexer run of 2026-07-28 07:04 logged `root=/tmp/analyser-src-451921075 files_read=543 file_read_errors=0 bodies_sliced=4536 slice_errors=0` -- out.Root was carried forward and was a readable local directory, in production, four hours ago.

guardian (medium, edit 1) asked for the READERS of code_symbols.kind, having noted I checked writers only. Enumerated: no reader enumerates kinds. diagnose_code_lookup never SELECTs kind at all (its three queries take path/symbol/signature/line_start/line_end/commit_sha, body/content, and the freshness columns). scanCodeSymbolRows in code_symbols_actions.go does SELECT kind and puts it in the lookup_code_symbols result map. `grep -rn 'case "func"' --include=*.go` and equivalents return NOTHING -- there is no switch or allow-list over kind anywhere. So the entire behavioural blast radius of adding 'doc' is: a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k, rendered as 'path :: symbol'. That is the intended effect, not a side effect.

plan.summary: ROUND 2. D11 layer 1b: index MARKDOWN sections from four durable prose sources into code_symbols, reusing the body column and content-search path layer 1 built. One row per heading-section. Requires relaxing code_symbols_kind_check, which permits Go kinds only. Round 1 corrections: the concept-register glob was measurably WRONG (caught 28 planning docs, missed 110 register entries) and is fixed; a ROLLBACK sidecar is added; the reuse search is done and recorded. Measured scope ~1,749 sections against 4,992 rows (+35%).

edits.rationale: code_symbols.kind carries a CHECK permitting Go kinds ONLY, so a markdown row cannot be inserted at all -- the mechanical blocker. Verbatim from the live DB: CHECK ((kind = ANY (ARRAY['func'::text, 'method'::text, 'struct'::text, 'interface'::text, 'alias'::text, 'type'::text, 'var'::text, 'const'::text]))). Adds 'doc'. READERS enumerated for guardian (round 1, medium): no reader switches on kind; diagnose_code_lookup never selects it; scanCodeSymbolRows selects it into lookup_code_symbols' result map only. NUMBER MOVES -- 253 is highest today, but this workstream's last migration was approved as 241 and shipped as 243 because two sessions took 241 and 242 inside four hours. Re-read the max immediately before writing the file.

ROUND 2, answering debug_historian (medium): the needle-gate discipline wants verify AND rollback as separate files, and this constraint relaxation is what makes the Go writer's INSERTs possible at all -- so a bad flattenMarkdown run had no scripted recovery. THE ORDER IS LOAD-BEARING AND IS THE WHOLE REASON THIS FILE IS NOT TRIVIAL: the old CHECK cannot be restored while kind='doc' rows exist, so the rows must be deleted FIRST or the ALTER fails with a check-violation on existing data. Written as one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable.

One symbolRow per markdown heading-section, from the checkout the indexer already has. Reuses symbolRow, the upsert/prune loop, embed-on-hash-change and body handling, so there is no second write path -- attaching the check prior_art_librarian asked for: `grep -rln 'INSERT INTO code_symbols' --include=*.go . | grep -v docs/` returns exactly ONE file, platform/orchestration/actions/code_symbols_actions.go. NOT REUSING chunkContent (rag_actions.go:396), answering reuse_agent: it is a fixed-width character window with overlap, not a heading splitter; a character window splits mid-section and destroys the heading->section mapping that is the indexed unit. IDENTITY: uq_code_symbols_identity is (repo,path,symbol); measured, in-file duplicate headings are rare but real (WRONG_CALLS.md 212 headings / 211 unique; 016b 130/130), so the suffix is required. Answering guardian (low): the counter is a per-file map[string]int incremented during ONE top-to-bottom pass over the file's own lines, so the Nth occurrence of a heading gets the same suffix on every run -- the order is the file's line order, never map iteration order.

content does THREE jobs -- trigram text, the EMBEDDED text, and the input to content_hash which is the re-embed trigger. composeSymbolContent keeps the code BODY out for exactly this reason; markdown must obey the same rule or the first reindex re-embeds all 4,992 existing rows plus the new ones. So content is heading + path only; the section text goes to body, which is what the content check now searches anyway.

Append markdown rows to the Go rows before the existing upsert/prune loop, so both kinds share one commit_sha, one prune and one set of counters -- the prune (DELETE WHERE repo=$1 AND commit_sha IS DISTINCT FROM $2) then covers markdown with no second reaper to keep in step. THE GLOBS ARE THE DESIGN, and round 1's defect was in them: the concept register lives at register/*.md (110 entry files), NOT at the top level (28 files, all superseded-by-design planning docs). Answering guardian (low, edit 4): the globs are config-overridable like defaultAnalyseExcludePatterns, so the scope discipline could be silently widened -- the VERIFY's out-of-scope assertion is the guard, and the Go comment marks the value load-bearing rather than a tunable.

A SUPPLEMENT, not a fix -- explicitly conceding editquality (low, edit 6): this file changes no behaviour and is not counted as covering any mechanism. It exists because 243's VERIFY caught a real defect in layer 1 that a reviewer had been asked to eyeball. Carries the 243 lesson forward: that file's EXPLAIN stayed pinned to the OLD predicate after the code changed, so it reported on a query nobody ran while presenting as coverage -- these assertions must be re-read whenever flattenMarkdown or the globs change.

plan.risks: (1) THE ONE INVARIANT, unchanged: content and content_hash must not gain section text, or every existing row re-embeds. composeDocContent is heading+path only; the VERIFY asserts hash integrity across ALL rows. (2) EMBEDDING COST IS REAL AND NEW: ~1,749 rows each embed once on first index. Layer 1's cost was zero-by-construction; this one is not, and it is stated rather than buried. (3) IDENTITY COLLISION: measured at 1 today. The suffix counter runs in document order over a single top-to-bottom pass, so it is stable across runs -- if a reviewer can show a path where it is not, the prune/upsert churns those rows every index. (4) SCOPE IS THE DESIGN AND ROUND 1 GOT IT WRONG ONCE ALREADY: the register glob pointed at 28 superseded planning docs instead of 110 register entries. That is the failure mode in miniature -- a wrong glob poisons the corpus with exactly the stale-doc class the plan exists to keep out, while every counter reports success. The VERIFY's out-of-scope assertion and the register_sections check are the guards, and the Go comment marks the value load-bearing. (5) BLAST RADIUS OF THE CHECK CHANGE, now enumerated rather than assumed: no reader switches on kind; the only behavioural change is that a doc row can appear in lookup_code_symbols' top-k. (6) ROLLBACK ORDER: the old CHECK is validated against existing data, so kind='doc' rows must be deleted BEFORE the constraint is restored -- the sidecar does both in one transaction so a half-rollback is not representable. (7) DEPLOY: Go is inert until the image rolls, so the CHECK relaxes immediately and markdown simply does not arrive until then -- a degrade, not a break. Confirm against the RUNNING pod with a string this change creates plus one it deletes, never git and never the tag. (8) The freshness banner keys on the indexed COMMIT (108 defect A, live v1.0.1189), so a prose answer carries the same staleness qualifier a code answer does.
